title: Helical Organization of Blood Coagulation Factor VIII on Lipid Nanotubes
protocol: Reconstitute human FVIII-BDD14 and porcine FVIII-BDD15 with HBS-Ca buffer.
Concentrate the reconstituted proteins to 1.2 mg/ml.
Store the protein solution at -80°C.
Mix GalactosylCeramide (GC) and phosphatidylserine (PS) in a 1:4 w/w ratio in chloroform.
Evaporate the chloroform under argon.
Solubilize the lipids in HBS buffer to achieve a concentration of 1 mg/ml.
Store the lipid nanotube solution at 4°C.
Glow discharge the Quantifoil R2/2 copper grids for 10 seconds at 50 W.
Mix FVIII and LNT solutions in HBS-Ca buffer at a 1:1 w/w ratio.
Incubate the mixture for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Apply 2.5 µl of the FVIII-LNT sample to the grid in the Vitrobot Mark IV humidified chamber.
Blot and flash freeze the grid for 3.5 seconds with a blot force of 1.
Store grids in storage boxes under liquid nitrogen (LN2).
Place the cryo-holder into the cryo-station.
Fill the Dewar of the holder and the cryo-station with LN2.
When temperature reaches -192 °C, open shutter on the holder tip.
Place previously frozen Cryo-EM grid into the designated place.
Secure the grid with a ring clamp.
Insert the cryo-holder into the electron microscope.
Refill the Dewar of the cryo-holder and the anti-contaminator chamber with LN2.
Wait for the holder to stabilize for 30-60 min.
Press F6 on and turn the filament on.
When the filament is saturated, press F6 off and open shutter on holder to view the grid.
Press Low Mag/alpha 1 (set at 200X mag) and locate areas with thin ice on the grid.
Switch to MAG 1/alpha 2 to set minimum dose (MDS) mode and acquire Cryo-EM data at low electron doses, without damaging the specimen.
Press F2 to set search mode.
Set magnification at 40,000x.
Enlarge beam with BRIGTNESS knob to minimal electron dose ~ 0.04 e-/Å²·s.
Press DIFF to switch to diffraction mode.
Set camera length to 120 cm with MAG/CAM LENGHT knob.
Locate areas on the grid within the pre-selected areas in LOWMAG that have lipid nanotubes in the holes of the carbon film.
Press F4 to set Photo mode at 40,000X magnification and set illumination with BRIGHTNESS knob at doses of 16-25 e-/Å²·s.
Press Standard Focus button to set focus conditions adjusting the Z-height of the specimen with the Z UP/DOWN buttons (RIGHT control panel).
Set defocus between -1.5 and -2.5 µm.
Align SEARCH and PHOTO mode by drawing a square in the LIVE VIEW window on the digital camera monitor in SEARCH mode corresponding to the area to be imaged in PHOTO mode.
Press F3 to set Focus mode at 100,000X magnification.
Focus illumination to cover the CCD chip (~4 - 5 cm radius).
Adjust defocus to ~-1.5 µm with the FOCUS knob.
Adjust defocus to ~-2.5 µm with the FOCUS knob.
Correct for astigmatism of the image with DEF/STIG knobs.
Select the FVIII-LNT to be imaged in SEARCH mode by acquiring live images in the LIVE VIEW window on the digital camera monitor.
Center the FVIII-LNT in the square drawn on the LIVE VIEW window.
Record a digital image on the CCD camera at 52,000X effective magnification and 0.5 sec exposure by switching to Photo mode.
Click the ACQUIRE button on the digital micrograph camera monitor.
Check the quality and defocus of the acquired image by pressing CTRL-F to obtain a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT).
Perform 2D image analysis with the EMAN2 scientific image-processing suite to select homogenous particle (helical segment) sets for helical reconstruction.
Select Cryo-EM micrographs with straight and well-organized helical tubes using digital camera software and visualization tools.
Invert the images in the e2workflow.py GUI, single particle reconstruction (spr) option.
Normalize the images for X-ray pixels in the e2workflow.py GUI, spr option.
Filter the images for X-ray pixel normalization in the e2workflow.py GUI, spr option.
Import the inverted, normalized and filtered images into the e2helixboxer.py GUI.
Select FVIII-LNT helical tubes and segment at 256 x 256 pixels with 90% overlap using the e2helixboxer.py GUI.
Evaluate the defocus from the original micrographs.
Apply contrast transfer function (CTF) correction to the helical segments, incorporating phase correction only, using the e2ctf.py option in e2workflow.py.
Generate initial particles sets in the e2workflow.py GUI - SPR option.
Calculate 2D class averages using e2refine2d.py with reference-free k-mean classification to select homogenous data sets of LNTs with the same diameter and degree of helical order.
Classify the initial dataset into 150 classes over 8 iterations, excluding particles with less than 80% similarity to the class average.
Merge particles from class averages showing pronounced helical diffraction using e2display.py to create an intermediate dataset.
Classify the intermediate dataset into 50 classes to differentiate classes based on diameter and degree of order.
Merge particles from classes sharing the same diameter and degree of order in e2display.py to generate the final dataset for three-dimensional reconstruction.
Perform a helical reconstruction with the Iterative Helical Real Space Reconstruction (IHRSR) algorithm.
Estimate the rise, Δz (Å) of the FVIII-LNT helix from the combined Fourier transform of the particles in the final data set.
Define the azimuthal angle ΔΦ (º) by running parallel IHRSR refinements with a constant Δz, increasing ΔΦ from 5° to 60° in 5° increments.
Run 100 consecutive IHRSR cycles for each final data set with a featureless cylinder as an initial volume and the initial helical parameters Δz and ΔΦ as defined.

Inspect the final volumes for convergence of the helical parameters and correspondence between class averages from the 2D classification of the final data set and the projections from the final IHRSR reconstruction.

Impose symmetry to the final 3D reconstructions, corresponding to the asymmetric unit distribution observed in the final asymmetric 3D volumes: 4-fold for the human FVIII-LNT and 5-fold for the porcine FVIII-LNT.
Run another 100 refinement cycles to generate a final symmetrized 3D reconstruction.
Calculate the Fourier Shell Correlation curve for both volumes by first separating the corresponding data set in odd and even using ‘e2proc2d.py <infile> <outfile> --split=2’.
Then run 100 IHRSR consecutive refinements as described previously.
Calculate the FSC of the 3D volumes created from the odd and even datasets using ‘e2proc3d.py evenvolume.mrc fsc.txt --calcfsc=oddmap.mrc’.
Visualize and segment the FVIII-LNT volumes in UCSF chimera.
Open the final volumes from step 3.2.5 in UCSF Chimera.
Set the contour level to 0.005 in the TOOLS > VOLUME DATA > VOLUME VIEWER option.
Select volume in SEGMENT MAP tab and click on SEGMENT to segment the volume.
Group segments corresponding to one unit cell by selecting with CTRL+SHIFT and clicking group.
Color the segments by unit cell and helix with ACTIONS > COLOR option.
Glow discharge carbon-coated 300-mesh copper grid (carbon side up) in a mixture of O2 and H2 gas for 10 sec at 50 W.
Apply a drop of 2.5 μl FVIII-LNT suspension with 6-nm colloidal gold nanoparticles to the grid.
Blot excess liquid from the grid.
Negatively stain by applying 5 µl 1% uranyl acetate solution for 2 min.
Blot excess liquid and air dry the grid.
Transfer the grid into the single tilt holder.
Transfer the holder in the electron microscope.
Collect tilt series automatically with the SerialEM software at 2° increments over an angular range of -60° to +60°.
Record images with a CCD camera at 52,000X effective magnification.
Maintain defocus between -6 to -10 μm during image recording.
Open the tomogram in 3DMOD using a terminal window.
Bin the tomogram by 4 with the IMOD BINVOL command.
Rotate the lipid nanotube along the Y-axis in the binned tomogram using the IMOD ROTATEVOL command.
Rotate the full tomogram with the IMOD ROTATEVOL command.
Crop the selected lipid nanotube oriented along the Y-axis with the IMOD CLIP RESIZE command.
Open the cropped sub-tomogram with 3DMOD.
Click on the tomogram to visualize the arrangement of Factor VIII molecules along the slices in Z-axis and along Y-axis in the sub-tomogram volume.
